Tip: to feed this meter to the Karoo, pair the sensor named “KPower: …” (your meter\'s name with a KPower prefix) in your ride profile — don\'t also pair the meter natively, or power will be recorded twice.

This only tells KPower which source the Karoo records as power (so it isn\'t duplicated in the FIT). You still pick the actual sensor in your Karoo ride profile. Estimated needs Comparison mode on; a real meter must be added on the Comparison tab first; External means another sensor you pair directly in the Karoo.

Records a detailed log file for each ride (every ANT+ page including unknown ones, parsed values, and connection events) so it can be analysed later. Off by default — it uses some extra battery and storage.

Only want dynamics, no power estimation? In your Karoo ride profile pick “KPower: …” (your meter) as the power source instead of “KPowerv2”, and leave Comparison mode off. The estimator then stays off — no estimation or weather lookups run.
No bikes yet — tap + to add one.

Exposes 4 estimated-power data fields and writes them to the FIT (est_power, est_power_3s, est_np, est_avg). For comparing against a real power meter. Off by default — increases battery/CPU and FIT size.

Reads advanced pedaling metrics (power phase, PCO, balance, torque effectiveness…) from the recorded ANT+ meter and writes them to the FIT. The Karoo does not record these. Needs a recorded meter. Live dynamics fields update only while recording.

Default surface (used if the map can\'t be read)

KPower reads the OSM surface under you from the offline maps (/offline/maps) and adjusts the Crr live (paved/standard/gravel/sand). Needs offline maps for the area and storage permission; otherwise it keeps the surface you selected above.

Headwind detected: KPower will take temperature, pressure and wind from it and skip its own weather lookups. Wind assumes Headwind\'s default unit (km/h metric / mph imperial); if you set it to m/s or knots in Headwind, wind will be wrong.
Headwind not installed: KPower will use its own weather (OpenMeteo/OpenWeather below).
